summary: A deep-half companion that separates three named exit routes from entry study and upper-body troubleshooting.
description: Navigate The No Gi Deep Half Guard 2.0 according to whether the problem is entry, exit selection or an opponent’s control.
overview: The outline introduces exits before surveying entries from several bottom positions. Its final volume separately addresses underhooks and chin straps, so a stalled deep-half exchange has a different study destination from a failed entry.

fits: You want to compare deep-half exits with the upper-body problems that appear in Glover’s troubleshooting volume.
consider_alternative_if: If half-butterfly entry and attack choices better match your starting position, compare Brian Glick’s guide.

includes: Overtop, backdoor and single-leg routes, followed by entries from knee shield and other bottom positions.
A final troubleshooting and drill block, including underhook and chin-strap topics.
limits: The entry collection is organized around reaching deep half; it is not a complete escape curriculum for every listed bottom position.

start_here.title: Separate entry trouble from control trouble
start_here.task: In the outline, compare the entry from the bottom position you encounter with volume 3’s underhook and chin-strap labels. Classify a recent stalled exchange as failure to enter or difficulty after entry. If you have access, study the relevant troubleshooting lesson before adding another entry to your notes.
start_here.section: Volume 3: The problem of the Under-hook — 0:59–7:01 (course range)
